blocks.content: The CAG of India is in reality an Auditor General rather than a Comptroller, having no control over the issue of money from the consolidated fund.

rows: No control over issue of money from the Consolidated Fund
Has full control; money cannot be issued without CAG's approval
Acts primarily as an Auditor General after expenditure
Acts as both Comptroller before issue and Auditor General after
Executive can draw money without prior sanction of CAG
Executive cannot draw money without prior approval of CAG

items: Distinction between Indian CAG and UK CAG: Indian CAG acts only as Auditor General, whereas UK CAG acts as both Comptroller and Auditor General.
Year of separation of accounts from audit at the Centre: 1976 (CAG still compiles accounts for State Governments).
Limitation regarding Secret Service Expenditure: CAG accepts the certificate of administrative authorities without inspecting detailed vouchers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The audit conducted by the CAG is mostly post-facto in nature, conducted after the expenditure has already taken place.
In 1976, accounting functions were separated from auditing functions at the Central level, relieving CAG of accounting responsibilities.
Secret service expenditure is a major limitation, as the CAG cannot demand detailed vouchers and must accept certificates from competent administrative authorities.
Unlike the CAG in the UK, the CAG of India has no power to control the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.
